subject.title: ci: add unsigned iOS build workflow

question: After the workflow hardening blockers are fixed, should OpenClaw core own a manual unsigned iOS archive workflow that publishes downloadable `.xcarchive` artifacts?
rationale: Code review can identify the required security hardening, but adding a maintainer-owned macOS artifact lane is an operational ownership choice for the project.

options.title: Harden And Accept The Manual Workflow
options.body: Keep the workflow as a manual unsigned archive path after applying the security fixes and rerunning successful artifact proof.

options.title: Keep It External
options.body: Leave the contributor's fork workflow as the distribution experiment and avoid adding this CI surface to OpenClaw core.

options.title: Defer To A Broader iOS Distribution Plan
options.body: Pause this PR until maintainers choose a first-party TestFlight, release, or sideloading strategy that this workflow can support.

recommendation.title: Harden And Accept The Manual Workflow
recommendation.body: Keep the workflow as a manual unsigned archive path after applying the security fixes and rerunning successful artifact proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is primarily about CI and security-sensitive workflow ownership, and recent history ties this area to vincentkoc.
